newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ADRs off in New York on nervousness.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ADRs off in New York on nervousness.

text.p: Foreign shares fell on Wednesday in nervous trading, and Latin American bellwether Telebras was off on unease about Brazil's economic and regulatory climate.
Traders said American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were largely lower, following the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The Dow was off about 100 points in late-morning trade.

"The prices haven't moved a lot, they are just reflecting the overseas down move" ahead of the New York markets' opening, a trader said. "Trading is nervous here but we're not seeing a lot of selling."

Telebras, Brazil's state telephone holding company, was off 1-3/8 to 75 following delays in introduction of a law that would regulate the opening of the telecommunications sector. A senior lawmaker said the bill was likely to be introduced on Thursday.
A trader said the decline also reflected concern over Brazil's trade deficit, with a private industrial group forecasting the gap would reach $5 billion this year, bigger than expected.
"Seventy-five is a pretty significant support level for Telebras," he said. "If it starts to go through there, the rest of the year doesn't look so rosy."
Among other ADRs, British Airways fell 3-3/8 to 97 after Panmure Gordon cut earnings estimates for the carrier. Finnish telecommunications company Nokia was off 1-3/8 to 56.
Declining issues swamped gainers by a 402-109 margin among an 807-ADR index. Volume was 31.6 million shares in late morning.
